summary: Graphene is the most likely identity on both metals, but the evidence is strong on Au and weak on Cu. On Au, a sharp G (1580.3 cm-1) and 2D (2681.1 cm-1) sit with a strong D band (I_D/I_G about 0.95 by height). The 2D is a single Lorentzian at 2.9x the G height (4.2x by area): monolayer-compatible, but below the ~4x rule and broad (FWHM 36.6 cm-1), so the layer number is not fixed. On Cu, G (1580.4 +/- 2.7 cm-1, height 22) and 2D (2695.7 cm-1, height 48) are present but close to the noise (SNR about 9) on a strong background. Two unassigned lines (2326 narrow, 2436 broad) do not fit graphene, so the Cu identification rests on the 2D-G pair and the matcher ranking rather than a clean G band. The spectra differ for three reasons, most likely in this order: (1) they are not directly comparable as recorded (laser wavelength missing, no Si or other calibration reference, different setups: MicroReactor vs UHV); (2) Au carries much more defect signal and has a higher SNR; (3) Cu has a stronger background and a lower signal. The 2D positions differ by 14.6 +/- 1.3 cm-1 while the G positions agree (difference 0.1 +/- 2.8 cm-1). A 2D-only shift lies outside the strain (slope 2.2) and doping (slope 0.7) directions of Lee et al. 2012, so it points to excitation energy (2D disperses about 100 cm-1/eV) or a 2D-specific change rather than substrate strain or doping alone. Resolving this needs the laser wavelength.

observations.evidence: rl_fit.py on spectrum_Au.csv (ALS baseline plus multi-Lorentzian least squares, covariance errors); fit_Au.png residual is structureless apart from a slight negative dip near 2600-2700 cm-1 where the baseline hump lies under the 2D.

observations.finding: Cu: G 1580.4 +/- 2.7 cm-1 (FWHM 22 +/- 9, height 22.3 +/- 5.3); 2D 2695.7 +/- 1.2 cm-1 (FWHM 37.8 +/- 3.8, height 47.9); unassigned narrow line 2326.2 +/- 0.6 cm-1 (FWHM 5.3 +/- 1.8, height 37.3, close to the 2.3 cm-1 sampling so under-resolved); unassigned broad band 2435.9 +/- 4.5 cm-1 (FWHM 48 +/- 26, height 22). I_2D/I_G about 2.1 (height), 3.6 (area), large uncertainty on G. No D band fitted.
observations.evidence: rl_fit.py on spectrum_Cu.csv; rl_qc.py flags strong_background (baseline swing about 200 counts, larger than twice the strongest band) and low_snr (9.4). Residual is noise-like, +/-20 counts.

observations.finding: Cross-spectrum: G positions agree (1580.3 vs 1580.4, difference 0.1 +/- 2.8 cm-1). 2D differs by +14.6 +/- 1.3 cm-1 (Cu higher). 2D-G separation: Au 1100.8 +/- 1.0 cm-1; Cu 1115.2 +/- 2.9 cm-1. Neither file has a Si line, so no calibration correction was applied.
observations.evidence: rl_series.py on both files (bands matched within 6 cm-1); notes from the tool: 'Au: no Si line found, not calibration-corrected'; 'Cu: no Si line found, not calibration-corrected'.

observations.finding: Physical reading of the 2D-only offset: the Lee et al. 2012 vector analysis gives strain slope 2.2 and hole-doping slope 0.7. A 2D-only shift at fixed G is in neither direction, so it is not a clean strain or doping signature. 2D disperses about 100 cm-1/eV while G does not disperse in stage 1, so a 15 cm-1 offset is equivalent to about 0.15 eV of laser energy. A turbostratic stack would also upshift 2D, but the Cu 2D width (38) is not about twice the Au width (37), which argues against turbostratic stacking.
observations.evidence: Comparison of the measured slopes and offsets in the Lee 2012 vector scheme with the dispersion values in graphene.md; the Lee analysis itself is valid only at 514 nm.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2012, Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (arXiv 1209.0234), p.3 Fig. 2 and p.5; Cancado et al. 2011, Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (arXiv 1105.0175), p.5; Ferrari and Basko 2013, Nat. Nanotechnol. 8, 235 (arXiv 1306.5856), p.7

observations.finding: Defect distance on Au from I_D/I_G = 0.95: L_D = 11.5 +/- 1.6 nm at an assumed 514.5 nm, and 17.4 +/- 2.4 nm at an assumed 632.8 nm. The laser is not recorded. The low-defect branch is assumed; the D width (34) is comparable to the G width (25), which the notes assign to the high-defect branch, where L_D would be below 3 nm.
observations.evidence: rl.py apply_relation graphene_defect_distance_from_ID_IG with I_D/I_G 0.950 at 514.5 and 632.8 nm.
observations.source: Cancado et al. 2011, Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (arXiv 1105.0175), Eqs. 3-6 and validity p.4; branch rule from graphene.md (Cancado 2011 abstract; Ferrari and Basko 2013 p.10)

observations.finding: Layer class on Au: the tool returns monolayer with 'high' confidence from one 2D component, but it does not use the 2D/G ratio or the width. The ratio (2.9 in height) is below the approximately 4x monolayer value and the FWHM (37) is broad, so I downgrade to moderate. Cu layer class cannot be assigned because G is too weak.
observations.evidence: rl.py apply_relation graphene_layers_from_2D_shape with n_2D_components = 1 and I_2D/I_G = 2.86 (Au) and 2.15 (Cu). The tool result did not change with the ratio.
observations.source: Ferrari et al. 2006, PRL 97, 187401 (arXiv cond-mat/0606284), p.2 (single sharp 2D about 4x G); FWHM(2D) above about 22 cm-1 typical on SiO2, Neumann et al. 2015 (arXiv 1406.7771), p.2

observations.finding: Library matching ranks graphene first on both: Au score 0.80 (G 1580.3 vs ref 1583.2, 2D 2681.1 vs ref 2679.6); Cu score 0.48 (G 1580.4 vs ref 1587.9, 2D 2695.7 vs ref 2687.6). The Cu G is about 7 cm-1 below the table value, within the calibration range the notes report but weak in signal. No DFT candidate matches the strong 2D on Au; the next Cu candidate scores 0.29 and only matches the narrow 2326 line.
observations.evidence: rl.py match_library, two calls (Au peaks; Cu peaks including 2326 and 2436).
observations.source: literature table lit:graphene, Lee et al. 2012 (arXiv 1209.0234); CRD entries from Bagheri and Komsa 2023, Sci. Data 10, 80

observations.finding: Unassigned Cu lines: the narrow 2326.2 cm-1 line is 5 cm-1 below the N2 vibrational Q-branch (about 2331 cm-1), so it is plausibly atmospheric N2 if the Cu setup has a calibration offset of about -5 cm-1, which is inside the 5 to 7 cm-1 range reported for uncalibrated setups. It is not a spike (rl_qc found none). The broad 2436 cm-1 band has no graphene assignment.
observations.evidence: Position comparison; rl_qc found no spikes; match_library gives the 2326 line only a weak CRD match (score 0.29).
observations.source: Calibration range from artifacts.md (Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024, 2012); N2 position is general spectroscopic knowledge, not from the skill notes

observations.finding: Both spectra sit on broad backgrounds. Au baseline rises from about 1000 to 1500 counts with a hump near 2650 cm-1; Cu baseline rises from about 620 to 820 counts with a hump near 1900 cm-1. Metal luminescence or fluorescence is a plausible source, not verified here. Baseline choice also changes the Cu G and Au 2D amplitudes.
observations.evidence: fit_Au.png and fit_Cu.png (baseline curves); rl_qc strong_background flag on Cu.

caveats: Laser wavelength not recorded: 2D and D positions disperse with excitation energy (about 100 and 52 cm-1/eV), so the 14.6 cm-1 2D offset between the two spectra cannot be read as strain or doping. L_D values are at assumed wavelengths (514.5 and 632.8 nm).

No calibration reference in either spectrum, so absolute positions carry an unknown offset (the notes cite 5 to 7 cm-1 for uncalibrated setups). The 2326 cm-1 line could be N2 (about 2331) after such an offset, but this is not established.

The two spectra come from different setups (MicroReactor vs UHV), with different background and probably different optics. Intensity ratios and widths are not directly comparable across the two; the Au and Cu comparison is qualitative.
The Cu G band is weak (SNR about 9; FWHM and position poorly constrained). Any Cu-specific conclusion about G, strain, doping or layer number is not supported.
The Au 2D sits on a broad hump in the baseline. A different baseline could change the 2D area and width noticeably; the height ratio is less sensitive than the area ratio.

The Au L_D result sits near the 10 nm validity edge and on the branch boundary: a D width comparable to the G width points to the high-defect branch (L_D below 3 nm), so the stage assignment is uncertain.
The layer-class relation returned 'monolayer, high confidence' for both spectra but ignores the 2D/G ratio and width. I did not accept that confidence for Au.

Expectations about graphene on Au versus Cu (work function, doping direction, thermal-expansion strain on cooling from growth) are general physics knowledge. They are not in the skill notes, were not checked against a source here, and are not used in the numbers above.
No literature search was run (Valency and iopic-bond unused). Citations come from the skill's graphene reference note and the matcher's literature table.
Files written into the data folder: fit_Au.png and fit_Cu.png (per-spectrum fit plots), series.png (two-spectrum overlay), peaks.json (holds the Cu fit, the last rl_fit run).
questions_for_user: What laser wavelength and power at the sample were used for each setup? The 2D offset (14.6 cm-1) and the L_D values depend on it, and the Lee 2012 strain-doping analysis is valid only at 514 nm.
Is there a calibration reference (Si, neon lamp, or a known line) for each spectrum? Without one the 2326 cm-1 line and the absolute G and 2D positions cannot be checked.
Are the two spectra from the same instrument and grating? Setup differences (MicroReactor vs UHV) would explain part of the background and signal differences.
Was the Cu spectrum acquired in air, or after transfer? A 2331 cm-1 N2 line would be expected in that case and could explain the 2326 cm-1 line.

Can you record a bare-metal spectrum (Au droplet and Cu droplet with no graphene) under identical conditions? That would separate metal background and luminescence from graphene and show whether the 2436 cm-1 band is intrinsic to the metal.

Is the Au D band from grain boundaries, wrinkles or point defects? Mapping the D/G ratio across the droplet would show whether the high D/G is local or global, and would help decide between the stage-1 and stage-2 defect branches.
How long was the Cu integration? A longer acquisition would test whether a D band is absent or just below the current detection limit, and would firm up the Cu G position and width.

Does the growth history (ethylene flux, temperature, cooling rate) differ in a way that would give a different number of layers or more multilayer patches on Au? Spectra at several spots would show whether the Au 2D width and layer class vary.
citations: Ferrari et al. 2006, Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 187401 (arXiv cond-mat/0606284), p.2 and Fig. 2: single sharp 2D about 4x G for monolayer; 2D shape vs layer number.
Ferrari and Basko 2013, Nat. Nanotechnol. 8, 235 (arXiv 1306.5856): 2D dispersion (p.7); turbostratic single 2D about twice as wide and upshifted (p.9); stage 1 vs stage 2 defects (p.10).
Cancado et al. 2011, Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (arXiv 1105.0175): L_D relation Eqs. 3-6 (p.4), validity p.4; D dispersion about 52 cm-1/eV and 2D about 100 cm-1/eV (p.5); FWHM(G) vs L_D (Fig. 5c).

Lee, Ahn, Shim, Lee, Ryu 2012, Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (arXiv 1209.0234): strain-doping vector origin (1581.6, 2676.9 cm-1) at 514 nm (p.4); strain slope 2.2 and doping slope 0.70 (p.5, Figs. 2-3); 514 nm validity (p.9).
Neumann et al. 2015, Nat. Commun. 6, 8429 (arXiv 1406.7771), p.2 Fig. 1h: FWHM(2D) above about 22 cm-1 typical on SiO2.
Bagheri and Komsa 2023, Sci. Data 10, 80 (Computational Raman Database): CRD candidates returned by match_library (not used for the graphene assignment).
limits: Laser wavelength not recorded: positions, L_D and the strain-doping decomposition are conditional on assumed values (514.5 and 632.8 nm); the strain-doping decomposition was not applied because it is valid only at 514 nm.
No calibration reference in either spectrum: absolute positions have an unknown offset. Shifts below about 5 cm-1 cannot be called significant across the two setups.
The Cu spectrum is near the noise floor: G position and width, the D-band limit and the Cu layer class are not determined.

Relation outputs: the layer relation ignores the 2D/G ratio and width, so its 'high' confidence was not accepted. The L_D relation assumes the low-defect branch; a D width comparable to G points to the high-defect branch.

What the data cannot tell: whether the Au D band comes from edges, grain boundaries or point defects; whether the Au 2D width (37) reflects strain, doping, multilayer patches or the baseline; whether the Cu 2436 band is intrinsic; whether the 2326 line is atmospheric N2 or a plasma line.

Rejected or not supported: the Cu spectrum as a clean monolayer (no clean G); the Au spectrum as a definite monolayer (ratio below 4x and broad 2D); a turbostratic stack for Cu (2D width not about twice the Au width); the strain-doping reading from the G-2D vector (laser unknown).

No literature search (Valency and iopic-bond unused). Expectations about graphene on Au versus Cu (work function, doping direction, thermal-expansion strain) are unsourced physics and not used in the numbers.
